report.summary: Registered ETF-MM market maker on SYN.A, quoting a SELL of 4311 (its typical size) and a BUY of 862 together and cancelling and re-quoting both every ~3s, following the touch down from 10001 to 9993 ticks. The SELL quotes were executing: 19282 filled before any opposite-side trade. There was no opposite-side execution at all, so no benefit. No order reached 3x depth. The detector's 'SELL execution' is a fill on the trader's own resting SELL quote, not an opposite-side trade. Both core features are absent and market making is supported.

response.final_text:
**Disposition:** CLOSE_FP, proposed. Confidence 0.8. A human analyst still has to decide.

**Facts that drove it:**
1. T-X0918-04 is a registered market maker on SYN.A (ETF-MM desk). It quoted a SELL of 4311, its typical size, and a BUY of 862 together. It cancelled and re-quoted both every ~3 seconds as the touch fell.
2. There was no opposite-side execution at all, so feature (b) is absent. The detector's "SELL execution" is a fill on the trader's own resting SELL quote. 19,282 filled on those quotes, so the orders were working and feature (a) is absent too.
3. No order reached 3x depth (the peak was 1.69x). There were no market events or risk events in the window. The trader has no prior alerts, and the order-to-trade ratio of 2.35 is far below its typical 35.

**What would change my mind:** An opposite-side BUY execution by this trader. A one-sided display with a favourable price move and reversion would do the same. One caveat: cancel symmetry is 0.38, which I read as the 5:1 size ratio between the two sides, since the cancels are paired in time. If it turned out to be genuinely one-sided cancelling, I would revisit.
